edit.description: manifest_write_findings (945-1003) reads `input.get("content")` (953: `let content = input.get("content").and_then(JsonValue::as_str)?;`) and returns `None` — no manifest verdict at all — whenever the field is absent, which is every `Edit`/`MultiEdit` payload (those carry `old_string`/`new_string`, or an `edits` array, never whole-file `content`). Now that GH #40 lists a co-owned manifest like `.claude/settings.json` as emit-owned, that `None` falls through at main.rs:359 to the blanket `.claude/ is projected` denial for ANY Edit to the manifest, even one touching only unmodeled residue (`autoMemoryEnabled`, `permissions.allow`) — legitimate under the co-owned posture and allowed pre-GH-#40. Add an Edit/MultiEdit path: when `content` is absent but `old_string`/`new_string` (or `edits`) are present, read `root.join(file_path)` off disk, apply the edit(s) in sequence, and run the resulting text through the same manifest-parse-and-validate path `manifest_write_findings` already runs for `content`. When the on-disk file is unreadable, or an `old_string` does not match (so the edit cannot be honestly applied), fall back to a manifest-specific denial naming the governed members and pointing the author at `Write` for a full-manifest change — never the wholesale `.claude/ is projected` message, and never a silent allow. The whole fix lands inside this function: main.rs:359 already treats a `Some` verdict as authoritative and needs no edit.

Add a regression: an `Edit` payload touching only an unmodeled/opaque key of a represented manifest (e.g. `.claude/settings.json`'s `autoMemoryEnabled`) passes `guard` (matching pre-GH-#40 behavior); a second asserting an `Edit` whose `old_string` cannot be found on disk denies with the manifest-specific message, not the blanket projection one.

summary: A co-owned manifest (.claude/settings.json) refuses every Edit/MultiEdit wholesale, even one touching only unmodeled residue, because manifest_write_findings only understands whole-file Write content.

per.section: The placements and their enforcement modes

tests.asserts: an Edit to a represented manifest touching only opaque/unmodeled residue passes guard; an Edit that cannot be honestly applied (old_string not found) denies with a manifest-specific message, never the blanket .claude/-projected denial

acceptance: Edit and Write share one rule for a represented manifest: a write (of either shape) touching only opaque residue or conforming members passes; one that drops a lock-declared member or cannot be reconstructed denies with a message naming the governed members and pointing at Write, never the blanket .claude/-projected wording GH #40 now emits for every manifest Edit.

edit.description: emit_one's banner branch (~2338-2348, added by bccf42c0's move from install to emit) only places the managed-projection banner, and only for a frontmatterless markdown projection (`projection.fields.is_empty()`). It never places the frontmatter `#` note — only install.rs's project_note (~1925) does, and only when frontmatter already exists. Since emit owns a represented projection's bytes in full (pipeline.md "Emit"; no file is part-authored, part-emitted), extend emit to place the note too for any markdown projection that carries frontmatter, so a freshly emitted projection needs no separate `install` run to converge its note.

Narrow project_note (:1953-1968) to the converge_banner_wording contract the banner already follows: None when no note line is present, converge-only when one is — the same narrowing bccf42c0 did for the banner. Move NOTE_COMMENT (still src/install.rs:205) to src/placement.rs beside BANNER (placement.rs:23), its one home; install and emit then read one constant rather than emit reaching into install's private module.

Regression: deleting a built-in skill's SKILL.md (or any frontmatter-bearing modeled projection) then running `emit` alone produces a projection carrying its note; `check`'s gate_installed (src/install.rs:561) reports no install.gate-installed finding without a separate `install` run.

Home for NOTE_COMMENT, relocated from src/install.rs:205 beside BANNER (:23) and BANNER_MARKER (:16) — the frontmatter note and the markdown banner are one placement family with one owner, so emit's writer and install's converger read the same constant (engineering.md, 'One job, one home'). Its unit test block (`mod tests`, :99) gains the note's own placement_lines case.

Two existing tests assert the OLD ownership split and must invert with this entry, not after it (build's own fence capture at 1e663552). (a) emit_never_stamps_the_managed_by_note (:1818) asserts the exact negation of this entry's acceptance — re-cut to assert emit DOES stamp the note and still never stamps the yaml-language-server modeline, which stays install's. (b) gate_installed_names_drifted_un_noted_files (:1097) hand-deletes the note line from an emit-owned SKILL.md and expects a missing-placement finding; under the narrowed project_note that hand-edit is drift by hash, exactly as this test's own sibling comment already says of the banner — re-cut to a stale-WORDING drift (splice a retired note wording in), which is what project_note still converges.

edit.description: Declaration rows for a layout source come from exactly two paths: emit over the program's declared members (drift.rs derive_layout_rows) and check's read-time derivation for local-locus kinds only (compose.rs local_document_rows). A discovered committed member of a layout kind that the program never declares is read at check for its field slots (compose.rs layout_unit) and for nothing else: coverage prints `invariant (0)`, explain says "Nested members: none", every leaf address fails, and no finding names the cause. Add a finding, advisory (config.stale posture), when a discovered committed layout-kind member has no matching provenance row in the lock — naming the two remedies: declare it in the program and re-emit, or declare the kind local.
The new finding sits beside config_stale (~2643) — the freshness-fact family the gate already reads disk-vs-lock through — rather than a second comparison mechanism.

Regression: a committed layout-kind document discovery finds but the program's member list omits produces the new advisory finding naming the file and remedy, rather than reading as zero coverage with no explanation.

gate() (~496-521) is where every advisory family already wires in (install::gate_installed, coverage_note::check, drift::config_stale_from_doc) — the new finding joins that same call chain rather than being reachable from check.rs alone.

summary: A committed layout document discovery finds but the program never declares yields no declaration rows anywhere — coverage, explain, and leaf addresses all read silently empty, no finding names why.

tests.asserts: a discovered committed member of a layout kind with no provenance row in the lock surfaces an advisory finding naming the file and the remedy, instead of reading as silent zero coverage

acceptance: check reports a discovered layout-kind member absent from the lock's declaration rows as a named advisory finding; the pipeline.md split (the gate reads declarations from the lock family and nowhere else, local locus excepted) stays intact — the fix is the finding, not new read-time derivation for committed sources. Per 0048's conservation bar, the regression pins non-vacuity: it asserts a non-zero count of discovered committed members judged before checking the advisory finding, so the test cannot pass over an empty read.

edit.description: New well-formedness check beside nested_member_admissibility (~60-79, the real neighbor — not satisfies_label_admissibility, which judges a different, host-blind ambiguity): a single host declaring the SAME (kind, key) nested member twice is a malformed lock, refused at admissibility. Two DIFFERENT hosts sharing a (kind, key) are NOT coincident under 0049's grammar (`spec:alpha/invariant/x` and `spec:beta/invariant/x` are distinct addresses) — that case is a resolution-time ambiguity, not an admissibility refusal; see graph.rs below.

`member_named` (:1650) is the ONE membership lookup `resolves` (:1632), `edge_resolves` and `member_at` all read since ab500f80 consolidated them, and its own doc comment already names this entry's ruling as owed: a bare key `also names an embedded member, taking whichever member of the kind carries it first ... which of several same-keyed members it means is an open ambiguity, and refusing it is a policy decision owned elsewhere`. Decide it here. Because ab500f80 also made an embedded member's identity ITS ADDRESS (`compose::embedded_member_features`), the host is now read straight off `features.id` via `parse_nested_address` — no plumbing, no carrier to thread. When a BARE (unqualified) key matches more than one nested member of a kind across different hosts, refuse at resolution (a new graph.route finding) naming every colliding host; the full host-qualified address always resolves unambiguously. `by_kind`'s pooled per-kind Vec (compose::embedded_features_by_kind, :1139) is what pools the candidates a bare key sees.
explain's bare-name resolution needs the same ambiguity refusal as graph.route, naming every host a bare/explain name could mean — why_impl (~538) currently collapses same-kind matches to the first.

embedded_hosts_by_source (:572) is the last partial implementation of "which host owns this nested member": it builds a `(kind, key) -> host` BTreeMap off nested_member rows with a plain `.insert()` (:578), so a cross-host duplicate silently keeps whichever row inserts last, feeding mention_reachable's citation scoping. It also hand-parses the host address a fourth time (`row.host.split_once(':')`, :577) where `graph::parse_nested_address` owns that grammar. Read the host off the member's own address — ab500f80 put it there — and give this the same ambiguity judgment, rather than a third lookup with a third failure mode (engineering.md, "One job, one home").

Three regressions: (1) one host declaring the same (kind, key) nested member twice refuses at admissibility; (2) two different hosts each declaring a same-kind-same-key nested member: a bare/explain-name reference to that key refuses at resolution naming both hosts, while either host's full `<host-address>/<kind>/<key>` address always resolves; (3) the same cross-host duplicate reaching embedded_hosts_by_source (a body-carried edge citation scoped through it) is judged the same way, not silently mapped to whichever host inserted last.

summary: A duplicate (kind, key) nested member is coincident only within one host; across hosts a bare address is ambiguous at resolution, never silently picked.

tests.asserts: same-host duplicate (kind, key) refuses at admissibility; cross-host duplicate (kind, key) refuses only a bare/unqualified reference, at resolution, naming both hosts, across every bare-key consumer (graph::resolves, explain's why_impl, embedded_hosts_by_source)

acceptance: A host repeating its own (kind, key) nested member refuses loud at admissibility. Two different hosts sharing a (kind, key) are legal (distinct addresses per 0049); a bare or explain-name reference ambiguous between them refuses at resolution naming every host, while the full host-qualified address to either always resolves. The refusal matches the SDK's, which SHIPPED this same bar at c60ddd3f (sdk/src/emit.ts:337-347: names every carrier host and points at the whole `<host-address>/<kind>/<key>` spelling) — one verdict at both ends of the seam, not two wordings. The bar fires at every consumer of a bare key, not only graph::member_named: explain's why_impl and embedded_hosts_by_source (gate.rs) each name every candidate host too. The regression pins non-vacuity: each case asserts at least one real colliding pair is judged, not an empty read short-circuiting to 'no ambiguity' (0048's conservation bar).
notes: observed at ad10e8cb (GH #51 half); corrected at bf4b4168 (refusing every cross-host duplicate hard-codes the alternative 0049 rejects). Post-ship reconciliation 09-07, second pass: EMBEDDED-MEMBER-HOST-CARRIED-NOT-SMUGGLED shipped (ab500f80) — the fields-map smuggling this entry was to fold is GONE, identity IS the address, and the three lookups are one `member_named`. Strictly smaller now: the plumbing is done and only the judgment is left. scoped at 1f79d12a

edit.description: clauseRow's `field: predicate.field` line (~106) reads `Predicate.field`, which the `sectionContains`/`requireSections` factories (sdk/src/contract.ts ~170-205) never set — both stay `undefined`, so every section_contains clause on a kind compiles to the same stamped label and every require_sections clause likewise collides. Special-case this line for the two predicates: synthesize `field` from the row's own `section`/`sections` data already computed a few lines below (`${heading}.${marker}` for section_contains, the joined section list for require_sections) instead of reading `predicate.field`. Verified this is the sole fix needed: `src/contract.rs`'s `predicate_from_row` reconstructs `Predicate::SectionContains`/`RequireSections` from `row.section`/`row.sections` directly (~472-483), never from `row.field` — so `clause_label`'s five other callers (compose, engine, graph, roster, schema) and `predicate_from_row`'s round-trip are both already field-agnostic for these two predicates and need no change.

The existing label-collision test (a_lock_carrying_two_rows_under_one_label_fails_admissibility_loud, ~2907) proves the refusal only on a hand-written lock (via common::clause/write_lock), never through the SDK — which is why this collision was never caught. Add a regression that authors two section_contains clauses (and/or two require_sections clauses) with the actual SDK, compiled through it (reuse the wire_sdk_harness pattern from tests/emit.rs:1748), and asserts the resulting lock carries two distinct labels and both gate independently, plus a round-trip check that the reconstructed clause's heading/marker/sections match what was authored.

SDK-side regression compiled through declarations.ts directly: two section_contains clauses (and two require_sections clauses) on one kind produce two distinct `field` values in their compiled ClauseRow output — the SDK-compiled regression the gate-revert audit asked for, at the layer where the fix actually lands.

summary: A section_contains/require_sections clause's compiled label never carries its heading/marker/sections, so every clause of that predicate on one kind folds to one label.

tests.asserts: two section_contains (or require_sections) clauses on one kind, compiled through the real SDK, produce two distinct compiled labels and both gate independently
declarations.ts's clauseRow emits a distinct `field` value per section_contains/require_sections clause on one kind, never leaving it undefined

acceptance: An author can declare 'every invariant carries a Test' and '... a Standard' as two independent section_contains clauses on one kind without them folding into one malformed-lock label; the same holds for two require_sections clauses. Fixed entirely at the SDK lowering (declarations.ts's clauseRow `field:` line) — src/contract.rs's clause_label, its five other callers (compose, engine, graph, roster, schema), and predicate_from_row's row-to-clause reconstruction are all unchanged and unaffected, keeping the blast radius to the two predicates' own compiled rows.
notes: observed at ad10e8cb (GH #48); corrected at bf4b4168: claimed only the marker drops — wrong. Re-cut smaller at 3571eb18 (after gate-revert 8e4e6b63 widened clause_label across 11 files): the label is stamped from `row.field`, only `declarations.ts` need populate. Narrowed further this tick: predicate_from_row reconstructs both predicates from `row.section`/`row.sections`, never `row.field` — the note's contract.rs split-back step is unneeded, dropped; one-file fix. scoped at cadabd8e

Per 0048's conservation bar, the regression pins non-vacuity: it asserts the captured own-span text is non-empty before checking it resolves as a leaf.

edit.description: Add `relocate(base, delta)` beside the existing `kind()` factory (~431 — shifted from ~336 by f8ba355b's discriminated-union narrowing, verified on disk 09-07). KindFacts is now three inlined object-literal union branches, one per locus shape (~168-310), each already near-fully duplicated by design (that commit's own rationale: no intermediate named types requiring root-level exports). A spread-merge (`{...base, edgeFields: delta.edgeFields}`) should stay within whichever branch `base` already is and type-check as KindFacts without touching all three by hand — confirm this holds under real tsc rather than assuming, since a marker field no branch currently declares (e.g. `facts.relocates`) is exactly the case a discriminated union complicates; if it doesn't type-check cleanly, a side-channel marker (outside KindFacts) is the fallback, not a third duplication of the union. Mark the produced facts with a relocation marker (e.g. `facts.relocates`) so KINDS-IN-PLAY-NAME-COLLISION-REFUSAL can later tell a legitimate relocation from a genuine name collision.
SDK-side payload assertion: a relocated `rule` kind declaring an added edgeField emits the fact in its compiled declarations (no `as any`, no dropped field).

Rust regression: the emitted edge fact from a relocated built-in resolves a real graph.route edge — proving no engine change is needed, since edges are always read from assembly `edge` rows keyed by `from` kind (never carried on a kind row itself); `graph.route` isn't assertable from an SDK test, hence the split.

This file already carries the corpus's one existing relocation vocabulary — a lock-row `row_relocates_builtin` (src/compose.rs:1091) recognizes a same-named row as a legitimate built-in relocation purely structurally (format/unit_shape/registration compatible), with no marker field at all, and doesn't examine edgeFields either — so a corpus kind named `rule` with an added edgeField should already flow through that existing Rust-side path with no engine change (matching this entry's own claim). Before minting a new `facts.relocates` marker in the SDK, confirm it doesn't duplicate `row_relocates_builtin`'s concept under a second name; if the marker is genuinely SDK-layer-only (needed before compilation to a KindFactRow), name that distinction explicitly rather than leaving two same-purpose 'relocates' vocabularies unreconciled. Extend this file's relocated-built-in fixtures if a new end-to-end case is the cleanest proof.

summary: A built-in kind cannot take an added edge field; the SDK has no sanctioned relocation constructor and an as any cast drops the edge fact silently.

tests.asserts: a relocated built-in kind's added edge field is emitted, not silently dropped by an as any cast

acceptance: A corpus can add an edge field to a built-in kind (e.g. rule) via the sanctioned relocation form and have it resolve a real graph edge, checked at check and rendered at emit — no as any cast needed. No engine change required: overlay_builtin_kind (compose.rs:453) never needs to carry edgeFields, since edges never live on a kind row.
